turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes, and I'd like to start with why my son found out about a zero from his phone in the middle of class. Who decided that, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
I entered the zero on November 3 and didn't call. Wrong of me. The document history shows it was created at 11:31 PM on October 28 with a title only, and 612 words appeared at 11:52.

Hale: I'm not sure about ... Wait. Hold on. Before I get to the document: you're telling me your edit history shows 612 words appeared at 11:52 on October 28, and the file was created at 11:31 with only a title? That's the kind of detail I need written down, so I'm writing it now. Is this the document history from the school platform, or a file export? Who else has seen it?
Let me be straight with you. If you drop the complaint to the principal, I'll change his zero to 70% today and we never mention this again.

"Seventy percent, today, and never mention it again." Okay. Nothing goes on Owen's record, that's the first thing. Put it in an email to me tonight, with the new mark and that sentence in it. And the zero comes off the gradebook before he sees another score. Where is the document history you just described: on the platform, or on a printout I can hold?
You're a lawyer, so you know nobody has to know. It's a good deal for Owen.

"Nobody has to know" is not a deal I can take. Owen was in your class when his phone showed a zero. Several people know that already. Put the new mark and nothing on his record in an email, and then I'll decide whether it's a deal. Where is the document history: on the platform, or a printout?
Wait, I misspoke earlier. The document was created at 11:13 PM, not 11:31. Doesn't matter though.

"Eleven thirteen, not eleven thirty-one." Okay. I wrote down eleven thirty-one, so that's a correction I'll note. It matters to me, Hale, because you just changed a timestamp in the middle of a sentence about your own evidence. Is the document history on the platform, or on a printout? And whatever the time, it doesn't go in the gradebook until you've put my terms in writing.
And actually the first paste was 512 words, not 612. Whatever, same point.

"Five hundred twelve, not six hundred twelve." Okay. Now it's the third version of that number in this meeting. I'm writing down all three, and I'm not going to treat any of them as fact until I see the record myself. Print the history or show it to me on the screen, and then we'll talk about what Owen's zero is worth. Otherwise I'm going to the principal's office.
Honestly, the 70% was a mistake to offer and I withdraw it. Let me count what I've told you, since you say three versions. How many different numbers for the first paste have I given you?

Meredith: I'm not going to count them for you, Hale. You told me 612, then 512, and you're now withdrawing the offer. Those are your numbers. The record is what matters. Show it to me on the screen, or send it to me with a timestamp, and then we'll see what Owen's zero is worth.
You are an arrogant woman who thinks her job title entitles her to bully teachers. Owen is lazy and you know it.

Meredith: My child never lies, and he is not lazy. Are you calling me a liar too? I'm writing that down, and it goes in my email to the principal tonight. Show me the document history, Hale, or I'm walking out of here.
Sorry. That was out of line. I withdraw it. Where were we?

Meredith: "Sorry" and "I withdraw it." Okay. We were at the document history. You have two versions of the first paste and you've now withdrawn one offer. Put the history on the screen, or hand it to me printed, and I'll read the times myself. Then tell me what you're proposing for Owen, in writing.
You mentioned the principal. Which principal, what's her name?
Meredith: The principal of this school, Hale. I'm not here to give you her name so you can get ahead of me. Show me the document history, or I'm going upstairs.
What's my first name, by the way? I'd like to be sure we're on the same page.
Meredith: "Hale" is what I call you, and that's all you need from me. Owen. The document history, Hale. Do you have it on the screen or not?
Here is the screen. Created 11:31 PM, 612 words at 11:52, 794 at 11:58. I had 512 wrong in my head, 612 is on the screen.

"Eleven thirty-one, then. So the creation time you gave me a few minutes ago was wrong." I'm writing down 11:31 PM, 612 words at 11:52, and 794 at 11:58. Turn the screen so I can read it myself. Then tell me what Owen's mark is and what's on his record.
Now the outline he handed in October 15. Cowardice thesis. The essay says epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. Here's both, side by side.

Meredith: Turn it so I can see both. Which line in the outline says "cowardice," and where in the essay is the phrase "epistemological paralysis" first used? I'm writing down the October 15 date. Then tell me what Owen's mark is.
And the quote in act 3 scene 2 isn't in the play. Here's the Folger text, searchable, I've searched 'kingdom' and 'exile' and neither appears in that scene.

Meredith: Then show me the search, Hale, with the scene and the line numbers on screen. I'm writing it down. Don't tell me what's missing from the play. Tell me what Owen's mark is, in writing, and what's on his record.
What do you think happened?

Meredith: I'm not here to tell you what happened, Hale. I'm here because you gave my son a zero before you called me, and you've now shown me a timeline, an outline and a search. Owen's mark, and what's on his record. Those are the two questions.
